narrative.title: Two Pickers Closing in from Both Ends
narrative.scenario: A warehouse keeps its sorted roster of bin weights on a doubly linked rail, and dispatch needs every pair of bins that together hit an exact truck payload of `target`. Because the rail is two-way, one picker starts at the lightest end and another at the heaviest end, and they walk toward each other — advancing the light picker when the pair under-loads the truck and retreating the heavy picker when it over-loads. Every combination can be checked without ever comparing a bin against itself.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of n distinct positive node values forming a sorted doubly linked list, and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: A list of [value1, value2] pairs, each summing to target, in the order the two pointers discover them.

testCases.explanation: The closing pointers land on (1,6) first, then (2,5); both pairs sum to 7.
Only (1,5) hits the payload; the pointer walk stops once the pickers cross.

hintLevels: Level 1: The list is already sorted — pairs are formed by matching the lightest remaining value against the heaviest.
Level 2: Walk one pointer forward from the head and another backward from the tail; move whichever side pushes the sum the right way.
Level 3: Stop the moment the pickers cross (start value >= end value) — continuing would pair a bin with itself and double-count matches.
